title: Test-enhanced learning: Taking memory tests improves long-term retention
venue_or_status: Psychological Science 17(3), 249–255; primary abstract in PubMed
evidence_note: Prose experiments separate short-delay performance from delayed retention; testing outperformed restudy at delayed tests.
limitation: Student laboratory task; abstract reviewed, without statistical reanalysis.

title: The effect of testing versus restudy on retention: A meta-analytic review of the testing effect
venue_or_status: Psychological Bulletin 140(6), 1432–1463; primary abstract in PubMed
evidence_note: Abstract supports testing over restudy and larger benefits for recall tests; several explanatory accounts remain under consideration.
limitation: Abstract-only inspection cannot audit synthesis methods or establish a unique mechanism.

title: Feedback enhances the positive effects and reduces the negative effects of multiple-choice testing
venue_or_status: Memory & Cognition 36(3), 604–616; primary abstract in PubMed
evidence_note: Immediate and delayed feedback improved later cued recall and reduced lure intrusions compared with no feedback.
limitation: Multiple-choice passage task; abstract reviewed; no universal feedback-timing rule inferred.

title: Distributed practice in verbal recall tasks: A review and quantitative synthesis
venue_or_status: Psychological Bulletin 132(3), 354–380; primary abstract in PubMed
evidence_note: Synthesis of 317 experiments considers interstudy gap and final-test delay jointly rather than as independent prescriptions.
limitation: Verbal learning; abstract-level review; numerical schedules are not agent maintenance policies.

title: Spacing effects in learning: A temporal ridgeline of optimal retention
venue_or_status: Psychological Science 19(11), 1095–1102; published article hosted at UC San Diego
evidence_note: Methods, gap/results, and discussion sections inspected; fact-learning retention depends nonmonotonically on spacing and target delay.
limitation: Specified material and learning criterion; interpolated optima are not universal schedules.

title: Learning concepts and categories: Is spacing the enemy of induction?
venue_or_status: Psychological Science 19(6), 585–592; author-hosted published article
evidence_note: Abstract, results, and discussion inspected; interleaved paintings improved new-example classification despite preferences for blocked presentation.
limitation: Visual category task; spacing and interleaving are not fully isolated.

title: Similarity matters: A meta-analysis of interleaved learning and its moderators
venue_or_status: Psychological Bulletin 145(11), 1029–1052; primary abstract and institutional accepted manuscript inspected
evidence_note: Abstract, definitions, and theory sections inspected; benefits vary with material, category similarity, and learning task.
limitation: Complete methods and statistical adjustments not audited; no universal interleaving rule.

title: Inducing self-explanation: A meta-analysis
venue_or_status: Educational Psychology Review 30, 703–725; publisher abstract
evidence_note: Abstract describes 69 effect sizes across 64 reports and benefits of prompted self-explanation in multiple instructional conditions.
limitation: Abstract-only inspection; accurate explanation and cost-effective implementation are not guaranteed.

title: Improving students' learning with effective learning techniques: Promising directions from cognitive and educational psychology
venue_or_status: Psychological Science in the Public Interest 14(1), 4–58; published article hosted at Penn State
evidence_note: Summary, explanatory-technique framing, and self-explanation assessment inspected; applicability depends on learners, materials, outcomes, and implementation.
limitation: 2013 human-literature assessment; utility ratings are contextual and may evolve.

title: Encoding specificity and retrieval processes in episodic memory
venue_or_status: Psychological Review 80(5), 352–373; primary abstract and APA publisher preview through ResearchGate; DOI 10.1037/h0020071
evidence_note: Primary abstract relates effective cues to encoding operations and reports recognition failure for some recallable words.
limitation: Abstract and opening publisher preview only; no detailed methods inspected.

title: Buildup of proactive inhibition as a cue-overload effect
venue_or_status: Journal of Experimental Psychology: Human Learning and Memory 1(4), 442–452; indexed APA primary abstract; direct page failed to fetch
evidence_note: Indexed primary abstract describes controlled list experiments supporting reduced recall as more material shares category cues.
limitation: Abstract-only review; human list results provide no numeric tag or folder limit.

title: Source monitoring
venue_or_status: Psychological Bulletin 114(1), 3–28; primary abstract in PubMed
evidence_note: Framework treats origin judgments as fallible attributions using experiential features and flexible criteria.
limitation: Abstract reviewed; theoretical synthesis does not evaluate a software provenance implementation.

title: Illusions of competence in monitoring one's knowledge during study
venue_or_status: Journal of Experimental Psychology: Learning, Memory, and Cognition 31(2), 187–194; primary abstract
evidence_note: Paired-associate work examines misleading judgments when answers present at study will be absent during later recall.
limitation: Abstract-only inspection; human judgment mechanisms do not establish model calibration behavior.

title: Cognitive offloading
venue_or_status: Trends in Cognitive Sciences 20(9), 676–688; author-hosted published article
evidence_note: Definition, memory, and metacognitive-framework sections inspected; offloading changes demands and can have costs alongside benefits.
limitation: Cross-domain human review; long-term consequences and optimal strategy selection remain open.

title: Strategic offloading of delayed intentions into the external environment
venue_or_status: Quarterly Journal of Experimental Psychology 68(5), 971–992; author-hosted published article; online 2014
evidence_note: Results and discussion inspected; reminders aid targets, with distinct triggering/content functions and limited everyday-task external validity.
limitation: Constrained online tasks; limited naturalistic association does not prove broad reminder effectiveness.

title: The generation effect: Delineation of a phenomenon
venue_or_status: Journal of Experimental Psychology: Human Learning and Memory 4(6), 592–604; primary article via author's ResearchGate copy
evidence_note: Abstract and general discussion inspected; rule-guided generated words were remembered better than read words across tested conditions.
limitation: Constrained word tasks and small experiments; generation does not certify truth.

title: The generation effect: A meta-analytic review
venue_or_status: Memory & Cognition 35(2), 201–210; author-hosted published article
evidence_note: Abstract and moderator/discussion excerpts inspected; synthesis covers 86 studies and substantial variation by experimental conditions.
limitation: Historical heterogeneous studies; selective inspection, without independent statistical reanalysis.

title: Desirable difficulties in theory and practice
venue_or_status: Journal of Applied Research in Memory and Cognition 9(4), 475–479; author-hosted manuscript
evidence_note: Performance/learning distinction and desirable-versus-undesirable difficulty sections inspected; productive difficulty depends on learner capabilities.
limitation: Theoretical commentary, not a new experiment or universal difficulty prescription.

title: Retrieval practice versus elaborative encoding: A systematic and meta-analytic review
venue_or_status: Educational Psychology Review 37, article 100; published 30 October 2025; publisher abstract
evidence_note: Abstract reports smaller retrieval advantages against elaborative comparators and a feedback-dependent direction of benefit.
limitation: Subscription full text not inspected; moderator findings are not universal causal policies.

title: Research on the testing effect routinely conflates direct and forward testing effects: A meta-analysis of testing effects with free recall
venue_or_status: Journal of Experimental Psychology: Learning, Memory, and Cognition; online ahead of print 8 June 2026; DOI 10.1037/xlm0001634
evidence_note: Abstract distinguishes direct from mixed free-recall designs and reports larger effects where forward contributions can be confounded.
limitation: Abstract-only review; free-recall synthesis does not invalidate every retrieval-practice finding.

title: Whether interleaving or blocking is more effective for long-term learning depends on one's learning strategy
venue_or_status: Behavioral Sciences 15(5), 662; primary abstract and indexed primary discussion; DOI 10.3390/bs15050662
evidence_note: Abstract and indexed discussion report sequence-by-strategy interaction extending across delayed testing and retraining.
limitation: Artificial letter-string categories; complete methods not inspected; realistic educational transfer remains open.

title: Hierarchical retrieval schemes in recall of categorized word lists
venue_or_status: Journal of Verbal Learning and Verbal Behavior 8(3), 323–343; indexed publisher abstract; direct page failed to fetch
evidence_note: Indexed publisher abstract reports organized word-list recall advantages and weaker effects for recognition.
limitation: Abstract-only inspection; word-list presentation does not evaluate filesystem folder structures.

title: Mnemonic training reshapes brain networks to support superior memory
venue_or_status: Neuron 93(5), 1227–1235.e6; 8 March 2017; DOI 10.1016/j.neuron.2017.02.003; primary abstract and indexed author manuscript; direct PMC/Cell access failed
evidence_note: Indexed methods/results inspected: controlled six-week loci training improved word recall and related to athlete-like connectivity; four-month assessment re-encoded words.
limitation: Male training sample; constrained lists and network correlations do not prove general workflow or agent-layout benefits.
